title: Virtual Memory and Paging
analogy: Phantom Panda haunts a spooky crypt library. He has a tiny spectral altar (RAM) and infinite dusty catacomb vaults (disk). He keeps only the active cursed scrolls on the altar and summons others when needed. Summoning a missing scroll is a Page Fault!
concept: Virtual memory gives each process the illusion of a large, private address space. Memory is split into fixed-size pages mapped to physical frames through a page table. When a page isn't in RAM, a page fault loads it from disk, evicting another page if needed. Too many faults cause thrashing.

options: Accessing a page not in RAM
quiz.why: The cursed scroll Panda needs isn't currently floating on his spectral altar.

options: Constant swapping with little real work
quiz.why: Panda spends all night swapping heavy grimoires back and forth and gets no haunting done.
